message:
I run deliveries for a small furniture restorer and I've got a few things to sort for tomorrow.

Can you suggest a name for our new delivery van (staff vote, nothing rude)?

Tomorrow the van can't leave the depot before 08:30 and must be back by 12:00. Three drops, each takes 15 minutes to unload. Drop A has a delivery window of 09:00 to 10:00. Drop B is a shop that needs its delivery done before it opens at 09:30. Drop C is an office that won't accept anything before 11:00. Driving times: depot to A 30 min, depot to B 20 min, depot to C 45 min, A to B 25 min, A to C 40 min, B to C 50 min. The driver also needs a 30-minute break somewhere before 12:00. What order should he go in, and what's the timeline?

Could you also rewrite our delivery text so it sounds friendlier than "Driver arriving. Be in."? List three things the driver should check on furniture before handing it over. Should we give customers a paper delivery note or an emailed one? And define "proof of delivery" in a line for our new part-timer. One more thing: we're thinking of texting customers the evening before with a rough arrival time. Could you draft that evening-before text too, keeping it under 160 characters so it goes as a single message?
response:
**Van name**
My pick is **Dovetail**, after the woodworking joint. A few more for the vote:
- **Patina**
- **The Chiffonier**
- **Chip**
- **Old Faithful**

**Tomorrow's route: B → A → C**

This is the only order that works. If he goes to A first, he can't reach B until 09:40, after it opens.

| Time | Activity |
|---|---|
| 08:30 | Leave depot |
| 08:50 | Arrive at B, unload |
| 09:05 | Finish at B (25 min before it opens) |
| 09:30 | Arrive at A, unload (window opens 09:00) |
| 09:45 | Finish at A |
| 10:25 | Arrive near C |
| 10:25–10:55 | **30-minute break** |
| 11:00 | Unload at C (the earliest it will accept) |
| 11:15 | Finish at C |
| **12:00** | **Back at depot** |

Everything fits, but **there is no slack on the return**. A five-minute delay anywhere after 11:00 makes him late, and C's 11:00 start can't move. If you can, check with C whether he can unload a few minutes early. Otherwise, warn the depot that 12:00 is a best case.

**Friendlier "on the way" text**
> Hi [Name], it's [Driver] from [Business]. I'm on my way with your furniture and should be with you in about [X] minutes. See you soon!

**Three checks before handover**
1. **Condition.** Look for scratches, dents or finish damage from the journey, and compare against any photos taken before dispatch.
2. **All parts present.** Check for keys, shelves, handles, legs, glass and fixings.
3. **Function.** Make sure drawers and doors open smoothly and the piece sits level and stable.

**Paper or emailed delivery note?**
Default to email, with the signature captured on the driver's phone. It's easier to store and search, and you can attach handover photos. Offer paper to customers who prefer it or don't use email.

**Proof of delivery (for the part-timer)**
"A record showing the item was handed over to the customer in good condition. This is usually a signature, a photo and the time of delivery."

**Evening-before text (134 characters as written)**
> Hi Sam, your furniture from Ashby Restorations arrives tomorrow, roughly 9-10am. Any problem, reply here or call 01234 567890. Thanks!

Swap in your own details. Longer names will add characters, but you have 26 to spare. Use only plain characters: no emoji, curly quotes or long dashes. Any of those switches the text to a different encoding, which cuts the single-message limit from 160 characters to 70.
